name: backup_audit_normalise
description: Turn a backup or hypervisor job record into canonical events and say what was not understood. It reads two things and no more: the Proxmox VE and Proxmox Backup Server task index (UPID lines: node, pid, start time, worker type, id, user, then end time and status; a Backup Server UPID carries one more field, the task counter, and escapes its worker id, which the event shows unescaped with the written form beside it) with a Proxmox VE task log (vzdump log lines and the TASK result line) and a Proxmox Backup Server task log file (format pbs_task_log, tasks/<XX>/<UPID>: `<RFC 3339 time>: <message>` lines, the last one TASK OK, TASK WARNINGS: n, TASK ERROR: <message> or TASK unknown; built from the Backup Server source that writes task logs and its documentation, retrieved 2026-11-03, and not checked against a real export: format auto does not recognise it, because a timestamped line is no unambiguous signature, so the caller names the format; a line that is not that shape is counted unparsed and located; a log with no closing TASK line is partial; the category of a message comes from this tool's keyword table, as the documentation lists no messages; a time with no zone is not assumed UTC; the message text is not printed) and a Proxmox Backup Server configuration file (format pbs_config: datastore.cfg, prune.cfg, sync.cfg, verification.cfg or remote.cfg, a header `<type>: <id>` and indented `<name> <value>` properties, built from the Backup Server documentation page Configuration Files, retrieved 2026-11-03, and not checked against a real export; format auto recognises one only by its documented file name together with a first section of that file's type; each documented property is a settings record (section type, object id, property, value; keep-* also as a number, and retention_setting marks keep-*, gc-schedule, prune-schedule, notify and schedule), a section type or a property the documentation does not list, or a value off its shape, is counted unparsed and located and makes the answer partial, and so does a section that lacks a property the documentation requires; the value of a comment, of a password and of any property whose name says key, token, secret or credential is never printed, only its length, and goes to the text file of a secret_output job) and a Proxmox Backup Server data blob (format pbs_blob: an 8-byte magic that says how the payload is stored, a little-endian CRC32 of the bytes after the header, the payload; built from the Backup Server source, pbs-datastore file_formats.rs, data_blob.rs and manifest.rs, retrieved 2026-11-03, and not checked against a real datastore; format auto recognises the four magics, which no text file begins with; each blob is an event with its kind (uncompressed, compressed, encrypted, encrypted_compressed), size and CRC result; the CRC32 of an uncompressed or compressed blob is checked and a mismatch makes the answer partial, the CRC of an encrypted blob is not checked because the source read does not show the bytes it covers; an encrypted blob is identified and never decrypted, a compressed blob is identified and counted but not inflated (zstd is not in the standard library) and its payload is not read, and both make the answer partial; an uncompressed index.json.blob of up to 16 MiB is read as the snapshot manifest, one event for the snapshot and one for each file with its name, size and checksum, an entry that is not {filename, size, csum} is unparsed and located, and an unknown field is tolerated and counted; an uncompressed client.log.blob is read line by line as free text that is not printed; a truncated header or an unknown magic is named and not read), and an export of ANY product (CSV, JSON Lines, a JSON array or XML) through a mapping the CALLER declares, or through a preset this tool holds: which field is the time, the action, the result, the actor, the object, how the time is written and what each action means (category_map). The tool does not know a declared product and says so on every event. A preset is a named set of those mapping parameters kept as a reviewed file under presets/ and checked against a sha256 list in run.py (a changed preset is refused by its file name; the tool reads presets from its own directory only); product selects it (and preset names one where a product has several), the answer says `preset: <name>@<revision>` and carries the preset's provenance, a preset and a mapping of the caller's own are not mixed (mapping, category_map, result_map, time_format, columns, record_tag, delimiter, has_header and time_zone_offset_minutes are refused beside a preset), and a preset's mapping targets only the keys a mapping may name. The one preset today is proxmox_backup_client_snapshot_list, for `proxmox-backup-client snapshot list --output-format json` (a JSON array of snapshots; built from the Backup Server source, pbs-api-types SnapshotListItem, retrieved 2026-11-03, and not checked against a real export; the listing has no per-snapshot action or result, so the backup type stands for the action, every snapshot of type vm, ct or host is labelled backup_end, any other backup type stays other, and every result stays unknown). The JSON array reader (declared_json) reads an array element by element under the line cap, the file cap and the clock, never the whole file: an element that is not an object is unparsed, a syntax error or a cut file ends the read at that point and is counted and located, and an element over max_line_bytes is located and ends the read; anything after the closing ] other than white space is unparsed, located by character offset and not read; a key repeated inside one object keeps its last value (JSON parsers differ on this, and the tool does not report it). A product with no fixtures and no preset here (Veeam, Commvault, Rubrik, Cohesity, Acronis, NetBackup, vCenter and others) is `unsupported`: with format auto it is refused by name, and no vendor layout is ever guessed from a sample. Each event carries its file, line or record and byte offset, a category (from this tool's worker-type table, which is as the tool's author knows it and is to be checked against the product version, or from the caller's category_map; the raw action stays beside it), a result (ok, warning, error or unknown, with the reason) and a time read exactly as declared: epoch seconds are UTC by definition, an ISO 8601 time with an offset is converted, a time with no zone is NOT assumed UTC and stays raw unless a fixed offset is declared. An event says what a record says happened; it is not proof the operation took place as described, that a reported success was a usable restore point, or who did it. Lines are read a line at a time with a line cap; a CSV field is capped; XML is streamed record by record with every DOCTYPE and entity declaration refused, one record is bounded to 4 MiB of text and attributes (a record over it, or a field over 1 MiB, is counted and located, never read in part) and the reader stops when 16 MiB pass without an element or text ending; a declared field a JSON Lines or XML record does not have is counted per field, and a time or action absent makes the answer partial, and so does a declared time that never parses under the time_format given; aggregates hold at most 10000 distinct values; every line is an event, a blank line or a counted unparsed line (the first 200 are located by line and byte offset). Every answer carries `provenance`: for each format read, its product, source kind, what the reader was built from (schema_basis: vendor_documentation for pbs_task_log, synthetic_fixtures for the Proxmox VE and task index readers, caller_declared_mapping for a declared format) and validated_against_real_export, false for all of them. A Backup Server status `unknown` is the result unknown (this tool's mapping), and the worker id is withheld in both its forms (as written and unescaped) whenever either form is. One XML file that cannot be read (an encoding the reader does not know included) fails that file and the run goes on. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries; exit 0 means the engine ran, not that the examination is complete. SENSITIVE: a log message or an error text can hold a path, a user name, a token or a repository string with user-info. The answer carries structured fields judged as below and the LENGTH of the free-text message; the message itself and the originals go to $OUT/audit-values.jsonl, mode 0600, only with write_text: true in a job run with secret_output: true. A time basis is a fixed phrase (never an exception's text). every string the answer shows is judged by the field it fills, in three layers, with the boundary text that the Windows and macOS tools carry too (one text in all 16 carriers). (1) A name (VM, datastore, snapshot, storage, key), a path or file name, an identifier (GUID, VMFS volume id, naa./eui./t10./wwn- device id, VMware uuid, MAC, CID, number) and a simple value (an enum word, a version, a time) is shown only when it fits the plain grammar of its kind: letters of any script, digits, space and a short list of punctuation, at most 128 characters a name (a path is judged component by component), no user-info shape, no secret's name beside a value, and no chain of 16 or more characters made of random-looking pieces (a GUID, a hexadecimal id of up to 24 digits, a number of up to 18 digits and the well-formed ids of devices are plain; an iqn. or t10. id is shown as an id only when what it holds reads as a name, and a t10. serial of 17 or more hexadecimal digits is withheld); anything else is `<withheld N characters: reason>` (a path component by component), and its original goes to the values files only with write_text in a job. (2) Every other text (a host name, a description, an annotation, an audit action or actor, a message) is judged on a copy with invisible and formatting characters taken out and the escapes of such characters decoded: user-info up to the last `@`, token-shaped runs, prefixed tokens (ghp_, AKIA, glpat-, sk_live_, SG., AIza and others), a PEM key, a run of more than 18 digits, and the value after a name that says it is a secret (password, passwd, passphrase, pwd, secret, token, credential, api, access, account or private key, auth, pw, sig, sas, otp, psk; any case, glued or CamelCase) after `=` or `:`, after a flag that takes one (-password x, --token x, --api-key x, -auth x, set password x, enable secret x) and behind a placeholder (password=<redacted>x, or <redacted> x when x is built like a secret), in time linear in the length; a name or a path component that holds a secret's name and, glued or after a space, a value of 7 or more characters built like a secret (password-Zq7kP2mR, Token Zq7kP2mR) is withheld whole. In free text these shapes are still shown whole (2,000 random plants per shape, two samples of 1,000 with different seeds, with 95% Wilson bounds in the pack's changelog): `password-srv01-` and 8 characters, 100% in each of seven alphabets (at least 99.8%); with 14 base62 characters 63%, with 24 0.05%; `password-` and two groups of 4 characters, 100%; a glued `--master-key` and 8 lower-case letters 7.7%, 8 hexadecimal digits 0.8%, 8 base62 characters 0.2%, 14 or 24 base62 characters none in 2,000. (3) The serialised answer, every error answer and every paging-file row are read back and checked by a second check written apart from the first two; a string it finds suspect, or in which it finds a piece of a secret-shaped text that the first two left between two cuts, is replaced by <withheld N bytes: backstop: why>, its place is listed in boundary.replaced_at, and the answer is partial. The judging of one run shares a cap of 400 million characters and a time that ends 6.5 seconds after max_seconds: past either, a string not judged before is withheld by its size (a short plain word stays readable), the answer is partial and boundary.stopped_by names the stop. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP that arrives once the module has run as far as its shared opening blocks (before any argument is read and before any evidence is touched) ends the tool with one JSON answer (status partial, stopped_by_signal naming the signal) and exit status 128 plus the signal number, the answer being a shorter one that says so if the signal comes before the output block has loaded; one that arrives earlier, while the interpreter starts and compiles the file and runs those blocks, gets no answer. Only the exact names of the files this run made are shown as they are; an extension that is not 1 to 10 letters or digits is counted under (other extensions). A short password used as a name, a token under 16 characters in a name, a value of 6 characters or fewer after a secret's name, a value built like words, a name the grammar of a plain name refuses (it is withheld: a false positive), and the shapes listed with their measured rates in the pack's changelog are not recognised, so run as a job with secret_output: true. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates two files under $OUT, mode 0600, both created before anything is read: audit-values.jsonl (each event's free-text message, and the original of every name or value shown withheld or shortened) and backup_audit_normalise-values.jsonl (the original of every string the boundary withheld or replaced, one JSON line each: id, field, label, length, value); a file already there is refused by name.  A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 13: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

path.description: One export or log file (use paths for several)

paths.description: Up to 100 files, all read as the same format; a link or special file is named and never opened

format.description: auto (default: recognises only the Proxmox task index and vzdump log), pve_task_index, pve_vzdump_log, pbs_task_log (a Proxmox Backup Server task log file; always named, never recognised), pbs_config (a Proxmox Backup Server configuration file; auto recognises it by its file name and first section), pbs_blob (a Proxmox Backup Server data blob; auto recognises its magic), declared_csv, declared_jsonl, declared_json (a JSON array) or declared_xml; a preset sets it. Any other product is unsupported until fixtures for it exist

preset.description: The name of one of this tool's presets (proxmox_backup_client_snapshot_list): needed only where a product has more than one. A preset fixes the format, mapping, category_map, result_map and time_format: pass none of them

product.description: The product's name. A product that one of this tool's presets serves (proxmox_backup_client) selects that preset. With format auto, a product this tool has no fixtures and no preset for is refused by name; with a declared format it is echoed as the caller's label and not verified

mapping.description: For declared formats: which field is the time and the action (both required) and, optionally, the result, actor, object, host, job and message. CSV: column names. JSON Lines and JSON array: dotted paths. XML: child paths such as a/b, @attr or tag@attr

category_map.description: For declared formats: the raw action (case-insensitive) to a category: backup_job, backup_start, backup_end, backup_error, archive_created, restore, snapshot_create, snapshot_delete, snapshot_rollback, retention_prune, retention_gc, retention_remove, verification, sync, vm_create, vm_delete, vm_power, vm_start, clone, migrate, disk_delete, config_change, repository_change, login, task_end, other. An action not listed stays other, with its raw name

result_map.description: For declared formats: the raw result text (case-insensitive) to ok, warning, error or unknown

time_format.description: How the declared time is written: iso8601 (default), epoch_seconds, epoch_milliseconds or strptime:<format>

time_zone_offset_minutes.description: A fixed offset from UTC, in minutes, for times that carry no zone (also for the Proxmox vzdump log's 'Backup started at' line). Daylight saving is not accounted for. Without it such a time stays raw and time_utc is null

has_header.description: declared_csv: the first row names the columns (default true)

columns.description: declared_csv: the column names when the file has no header row

record_tag.description: declared_xml: the element name of one record

limit.description: Rows shown inline per list (default 200); every row is counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results; the rows shown inline also stop at about 512 KiB per list whatever limit says (pages.<list>.inline_cut_by_size), so that the answer is written within max_seconds and keeps its status: the rest is in the file

max_line_bytes.description: A line over this is located and not read (default 1048576, at least 4096)

max_file_bytes.description: A file over this is named and not read (default 8 GiB)

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 50, at most 50); what is left is named and the answer is partial

write_text.description: Write each event's free-text message, and the original of every name or value the answer shows withheld or shortened, to 0600 files under $OUT (the tool's own text file and backup_audit_normalise-values.jsonl) (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job that is secret output: the manifest declares it, so a job with write_text true is made secret by the job service whether or not the agent asked
